title: Subtree of Another Tree
statement:
Given the roots of two binary trees `root` and `subRoot`, return `true` if there is a subtree of `root` with the same structure and node values as `subRoot`, and `false` otherwise.

A subtree of a binary tree `tree` is a tree that consists of a node in `tree` and all of this node's descendants.

Build real `TreeNode` trees from both arrays, then for every node in `root`, check whether the subtree rooted there is structurally identical to `subRoot` (reusing the same-tree comparison).
constraints: The number of nodes in root is in the range [1, 2000]
The number of nodes in subRoot is in the range [1, 1000]

editorial.approach: Write a helper `same(a, b)` that checks whether two trees are structurally identical (like Same Tree). Then do a DFS over `root`: at each node, if `same(node, subRoot)` is true, return true immediately. Otherwise recurse into the node's left and right children. Return false if no matching subtree is found anywhere.
editorial.complexity: O(m * n) time in the worst case / O(m + n) space
